name: CSX
desc: Freight railroad operating about 20,000 route miles in the eastern United States, hauling coal, intermodal containers, chemicals and automotive goods.
markets: Shippers and ports across 26 eastern US states and Washington DC; no international operations or verified expansion plans.
rationale: Large US rail brand with B2B hospitality value for shippers, but domestic network and little consumer marketing give a weak fit.

name: Svenska Cellulosa Aktiebolaget (SCA)
desc: Swedish forest products group and Europe's largest private forest owner, producing pulp, solid wood, kraftliner and renewable energy.
markets: Sells pulp, wood products and kraftliner to paper, packaging and building customers, mainly in Europe with exports to other regions.
rationale: Sustainability-led forest group could use F1 for green-materials messaging, but it is B2B with little consumer brand profile.

name: Africa Trade and Distribution Company
desc: Strategic entity listed by Crunchbase under logistics and manufacturing; products, owners and location are not confirmed.
markets: Location, customers and markets are not confirmed in the data; the name suggests African trade, but this is unverified.
rationale: Too little is known to judge fit; no confirmed brand, markets or marketing activity, so F1 relevance is unclear.

name: Direct ChassisLink
desc: Leases and manages marine, domestic and international intermodal chassis, the trailers that carry shipping containers on US roads.
markets: Customers are US shipping lines, railroads and trucking firms moving containers; no verified operations outside the United States.
rationale: B2B equipment lessor with low brand visibility; some logistics-customer hospitality value but little marketing culture, so weak F1 fit.

name: DL Invest Group
desc: Polish group that develops and invests in logistics and industrial parks, mainly in Poland and Central Europe.
markets: Industrial and logistics parks for tenants in Poland and neighbouring Central European countries; no confirmed expansion beyond that region.
rationale: B2B property developer with regional tenants; hospitality value is modest and brand awareness is low, so F1 fit is weak.

name: GB Logistics
desc: Egyptian logistics company offering freight and logistics services, part of the GB Corp group.
markets: Appears to serve customers in Egypt; scale, services and any foreign operations were not confirmed.
rationale: Group-backed Egyptian logistics firm with limited known marketing; little evidence of international ambitions makes F1 a weak fit.

name: TFI International
desc: Montreal-based trucking and logistics group running less-than-truckload, truckload, package, courier and logistics businesses across North America.
markets: Operates through many subsidiaries in Canada and the United States, with some Mexican operations; customers are shippers across North America.
rationale: Large North American carrier with B2B hospitality use for shippers, but its multi-brand model and regional footprint limit fit.

name: SFL Corporation
desc: Bermuda-based maritime investment company that owns and charters out tankers, container ships, dry bulk vessels and offshore drilling units.
markets: Charters vessels to shipping lines, oil majors and drilling contractors worldwide; fleet has operated in several world regions.
rationale: Capital-intensive ship owner with few consumer or marketing needs; limited hospitality interest, so F1 relevance is low.

name: TUI Cruises
desc: Hamburg-based cruise line operating Mein Schiff ships for German-speaking guests, a joint venture of TUI Group and Royal Caribbean.
markets: Mein Schiff ships sail mainly for German-speaking guests in Europe, the Mediterranean, Caribbean and elsewhere; ownership shared by TUI and Royal Caribbean.
rationale: Consumer cruise brand with premium hospitality appeal in Germany, but MSC Cruises already holds the F1 cruise slot and reach is largely German.

name: ADNOC Logistics & Services
desc: Abu Dhabi marine logistics company with offshore support vessels, tankers, dry bulk ships and logistics services for the energy industry.
markets: Serves ADNOC and third-party energy and trading customers with vessels trading across the Gulf and internationally.
rationale: Abu Dhabi state-linked brand could use the Abu Dhabi Grand Prix for hospitality, though its business is B2B and energy-focused.

name: Gulf Navigation Holding
desc: Dubai-based shipping company that owns and operates vessels such as tankers and chartering and ship-management services.
markets: Gulf-based ship operator serving regional charterers; exact trading areas and customers were not confirmed.
rationale: Small Dubai-listed shipper with little marketing culture; some regional hospitality use at Gulf races, but weak fit overall.

name: Nordam Group
desc: Tulsa aerospace supplier and independent maker of aircraft nacelle systems, thrust reversers, interiors and repair services for airlines and manufacturers.
markets: Supplies and repairs components for airlines and aircraft makers worldwide, with facilities in the United States and abroad.
rationale: B2B aerospace supplier with strong engineering overlap with F1, yet low consumer visibility; value lies in technology showcase and hospitality.

name: Overhaul
desc: Supply chain integrity technology company providing real-time shipment visibility, risk management and cargo security for shippers.
markets: US-based software and services provider for shippers; international customers and expansion plans were not confirmed.
rationale: Technology provider with a data-visibility story that suits an F1 showcase, but small and unproven as a sponsor.

name: CargoBeamer
desc: Leipzig rail logistics company whose terminals load semi-trailers, including non-craneable ones, onto trains for intermodal freight across Europe.
markets: Runs rail freight routes between terminals across Germany and Europe for trucking and logistics customers.
rationale: Green rail logistics brand with sustainability storytelling, but small B2B scale and a European focus make F1 fit modest.

name: GreenLine Mobility Solutions
desc: Indian logistics company running heavy trucks on liquefied natural gas and offering lower-emission freight transport.
markets: Serves freight customers on Indian highway routes; no verified operations or expansion plans outside India.
rationale: Low-carbon freight story could suit F1 sustainability messaging, but India-only B2B scale and early stage limit fit.

name: Stolt-Nielsen
desc: Operator of chemical tankers, storage terminals, tank containers and fish farming, run from London and registered in Bermuda.
markets: Stolt Tankers, Stolthaven terminals and Stolt Tank Containers serve chemical and food customers across Europe, Americas and Asia.
rationale: B2B shipping group with global footprint and hospitality use for chemical customers, but little consumer brand marketing.

name: Wrightbus
desc: Northern Ireland maker of single- and double-deck buses, including zero-emission battery and hydrogen buses and the London Routemaster.
markets: Sells buses to transport operators mainly in the UK, Ireland and Europe, with some exports further afield.
rationale: Zero-emission and hydrogen bus maker could use F1 as a technology showcase, though sales are to operators, not consumers.

name: MTN Group
desc: Johannesburg-based mobile operator and one of Africa's largest, serving subscribers across about 20 markets in Africa and the Middle East.
markets: Consumer and business mobile, data and fintech services across Africa and parts of the Middle East.
rationale: Brand-led African telco with sports sponsorship history and growth interest in new markets; F1's African ambitions give hospitality and brand value.

name: Koiviston Auto
desc: Finnish bus operator based in Lahti running regional, commuter, express and charter coach services.
markets: Passengers and public transport authorities in Finland; no verified operations or expansion plans outside Finland.
rationale: Regional Finnish coach operator with limited marketing needs and no international reach; weak F1 fit.

name: Autoroute de Liaison Seine-Sarthe (ALIS)
desc: Concession company that built, operates and maintains the A28 motorway between Rouen and Alencon in Normandy, financed by tolls.
markets: Toll-paying drivers and hauliers on one French motorway section; no operations beyond this concession.
rationale: Single-road concession vehicle with no consumer brand marketing and no international ambitions; very unlikely sponsor.

name: Highland Electric Fleets
desc: Provider of electric school buses and fleet electrification as a service, handling vehicles, charging and operations for school districts.
markets: School districts and fleet operators in the United States; no verified operations abroad.
rationale: Electrification story fits F1 technology and sustainability themes, but US-only public customers and small scale limit the case.

name: Suncrete
desc: Dallas construction materials company providing ready-mix concrete solutions and delivery for contractors, builders and developers.
markets: Contractors and developers in Texas; no international activity or expansion plans known.
rationale: Local building-materials supplier with no consumer brand and no international growth; F1 fit is weak.

name: HUboo
desc: Denver company that Crunchbase describes as providing cross-border freight, warehousing and related logistics services.
markets: Based in the United States; Crunchbase mentions cross-border freight but customers and routes are not confirmed.
rationale: Little is known about the business or brand; a logistics provider of unproven scale with weak apparent F1 relevance.

name: New Jersey Transit
desc: State public transportation corporation of New Jersey operating commuter rail, buses and light rail.
markets: Commuters and travellers in New Jersey and the New York region; no international operations.
rationale: State transit agency with no commercial sponsorship need or international reach; government body and a very unlikely partner.

name: Ruiyun Cold Chain
desc: Chinese company providing temperature-controlled logistics and supply chain services; scale and customers are not confirmed.
markets: Appears to serve food and retail customers in China; no international activity or plans confirmed.
rationale: Unproven Chinese B2B cold-chain operator with no known consumer brand, so F1 relevance is weak.

name: Foodpanda
desc: Online food and grocery delivery marketplace owned by Delivery Hero, operating in several Asian markets from a Singapore regional base.
markets: Consumers and restaurants in South and South-East Asian markets; some markets have changed through exits and sales under Delivery Hero.
rationale: Consumer app brand with large Asian audience that could use F1 for activation, but ownership by Delivery Hero governs any deal.

name: Postmates
desc: On-demand delivery platform that brought food, groceries and goods from local restaurants and stores to customers by app.
markets: Operated in United States cities; acquired by Uber, which folded the service into its delivery business.
rationale: Brand now absorbed into Uber's delivery operations, so a standalone F1 partnership is unlikely.
changed: Acquired by Uber in 2020

name: Wolt
desc: Helsinki-based food and retail delivery platform letting consumers order from restaurants, shops and supermarkets across about 25 countries.
markets: Operates in Europe, Israel, Japan and Central Asia, now under DoorDash ownership.
rationale: Consumer delivery brand with wide international footprint and marketing budget, but ownership by DoorDash decides sponsorship choices.
changed: Acquired by DoorDash in 2022

name: Deliverr
desc: E-commerce fulfilment company that offered fast two-day shipping for online sellers by storing their products in a distributed warehouse network.
markets: Served online sellers shipping within the United States before being absorbed into larger platforms.
rationale: Brand no longer exists as an independent business, so there is no sponsorship counterpart.
changed: Acquired by Shopify in 2022; sold to Flexport in 2023

name: Dingdang Kuaiyao
desc: Online-to-offline medicine delivery service of Dingdang Health Technology Group, delivering pharmacy products to consumers by app in China.
markets: Consumers in Chinese cities; the parent is listed in Hong Kong and no overseas expansion is known.
rationale: China-only online pharmacy service with restricted health-product marketing; limited fit for F1 sponsorship.

name: Loggi
desc: Brazilian logistics technology company delivering parcels for e-commerce companies and consumers through a technology-driven courier network.
markets: Parcel delivery for online retailers and consumers in Brazilian cities; no verified operations outside Brazil.
rationale: Consumer-facing Brazilian delivery brand that could use the Sao Paulo Grand Prix for hospitality, though it has no international reach.

name: Navios South American Logistics
desc: Port and river logistics company operating the Nueva Palmira terminals, Parana-Paraguay barge and pushboat fleets, and cabotage services.
markets: Moves grain, mining and forestry cargo for customers in Uruguay, Paraguay, Argentina, Brazil and Bolivia.
rationale: B2B river and port operator with no consumer profile; limited hospitality value and regional reach make F1 fit weak.

name: American Express Global Business Travel
desc: Corporate travel management company that books and manages business travel, meetings and expenses for large organisations.
markets: Serves corporate clients across the Americas, Europe and Asia-Pacific, with travel advisors and technology platforms worldwide.
rationale: Business travel specialist with strong B2B hospitality and event-travel value and clear tie to an existing F1 partner brand.
f1: Operates under the American Express brand name under licence; American Express is a current F1 partner, but no own F1 deal is confirmed.

name: PayCargo
desc: Logistics payments platform that digitises freight billing so shippers, forwarders and carriers can pay and get paid electronically.
markets: US-based platform used by shippers, freight forwarders and carriers; extent of international use and expansion plans were not confirmed.
rationale: B2B payments tool with a logistics niche; F1 payment partners already exist and PayCargo has little consumer profile.

name: Rivigo
desc: Indian technology-enabled logistics company known for a relay model of long-haul trucking in which drivers hand over trucks.
markets: Road freight services for shippers across India; no verified operations or expansion plans outside India.
rationale: Indian freight business with B2B customers and limited marketing culture; little F1 relevance beyond India-only brand building.

name: Veho
desc: US last-mile parcel delivery company offering technology-enabled delivery that lets recipients choose the delivery time.
markets: Delivers packages for US retailers and brands; no verified operations outside the United States.
rationale: US-only delivery company with brand-conscious retail customers but no international footprint, so F1 relevance is limited.

name: Dian Xiaomi
desc: Chinese company providing one-stop services for global e-commerce sellers, including warehousing and logistics.
markets: Chinese e-commerce sellers using its services; details of markets served and any expansion plans were not confirmed.
rationale: Little verified information, no known consumer brand and no confirmed international marketing; F1 fit is weak.

name: Golden State Water
desc: Regulated water utility serving about one million people across Southern and Northern California, a subsidiary of American States Water.
markets: Water customers in California only; part of listed American States Water with no international activity.
rationale: Regulated local utility with no competitive marketing need and no international reach; very weak F1 fit.

name: Good Eggs
desc: Online grocer and meal kit delivery service sourcing food from local farms and makers and delivering to US customers.
markets: Consumers in the San Francisco Bay Area and a few other US cities; no international operations.
rationale: Small US grocery delivery brand with local customers and no international growth; weak F1 fit.

name: Floward
desc: Saudi online retailer of flowers and gifts such as bouquets, plants, chocolates and cakes, with delivery across the Gulf.
markets: Consumers in Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Kuwait, Qatar and other Gulf countries, with expansion elsewhere.
rationale: Gulf consumer brand with gifting occasions that could use F1 in Saudi, Qatar and Abu Dhabi for visibility.

name: FineEx
desc: Chinese e-commerce warehousing and logistics company described by Crunchbase as domestic in focus.
markets: China-based warehousing and logistics for e-commerce customers; no international operations confirmed.
rationale: B2B domestic logistics provider with no known consumer marketing; very limited F1 relevance.

name: Avianca Holdings
desc: Colombian airline group and national flag carrier Avianca, with a hub at Bogota flying across the Americas and to Europe.
markets: Passenger and cargo services across Latin America, North America and Europe, now part of the Abra Group.
rationale: Latin American flag carrier with big brand marketing and F1 races in Mexico, Brazil and the United States; Etihad, Qatar and others already sponsor.
changed: Combined with GOL under Abra Group, formed 2022

name: Didi Freight
desc: Beijing freight platform of DiDi offering on-demand intra-city logistics that matches shippers with truck drivers.
markets: Shippers and truck drivers in Chinese cities; no known operations abroad.
rationale: China-focused freight platform within DiDi with little standalone brand marketing; weak F1 fit.

name: Cryoport
desc: Provides temperature-controlled logistics and storage for the life sciences industry, including frozen shipping systems for cell and gene therapies.
markets: Serves pharma, biotech and clinical research customers across North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: B2B life sciences logistics with global footprint but a specialist customer base; modest hospitality value and weak F1 fit.

name: Yellow Corporation
desc: Former less-than-truckload freight carrier operating Yellow, Reddaway and other regional trucking networks before collapsing in 2023.
markets: Served US shippers with regional and national LTL freight; ceased operations in 2023.
rationale: Company ceased operations and filed for bankruptcy in 2023, so no sponsorship partner exists.
changed: Ceased operations and filed for bankruptcy in 2023

name: G7
desc: Beijing fleet management and Internet of Things platform providing telematics and data services to road freight carriers and shippers.
markets: Road freight carriers and shippers in China; no verified operations or expansion plans abroad.
rationale: B2B telematics supplier with data and technology themes, but China-only reach and little consumer brand weaken the fit.

name: Forto
desc: Berlin digital freight forwarder, founded in 2016 as Freighthub, offering ocean and air freight through an online platform for companies.
markets: Ships for businesses between Europe, Asia and North America with offices in several regions.
rationale: Tech-led forwarder with international growth and B2B hospitality value, though DHL and CEVA already hold F1 logistics roles.

name: Union Pacific
desc: Large US freight railroad running about 32,000 route miles in the west, hauling bulk, industrial and intermodal freight.
markets: Shippers across the western two-thirds of the United States and cross-border gateways with Mexico and Canada.
rationale: Major US rail brand with B2B hospitality value for shippers, but domestic focus and no consumer marketing keep fit low.

name: Giga Carbon Neutrality
desc: Chinese clean energy trucking and logistics business deploying electric heavy trucks and battery swapping for fleet operators.
markets: Fleet operators in China; no verified operations or expansion plans outside China.
rationale: Electric trucking story fits F1 technology themes, but it is China-focused, B2B and early stage.

name: Mobico Group
desc: UK shared mobility group, formerly National Express, running North American school buses and bus and coach services in Europe.
markets: School buses in North America, ALSA coaches in Spain and Morocco, and bus and coach services in the UK.
rationale: Large consumer-facing transport operator with sizeable passenger numbers, but mostly public-contract business and no clear F1 use.
changed: Renamed from National Express Group in 2023

name: Eneti
desc: Former shipping company, previously Scorpio Bulkers, that moved into offshore wind turbine installation vessels and merged into Cadeler.
markets: Offshore wind turbine installation vessels for European and Asian wind projects before merging into Cadeler.
rationale: Business no longer exists independently after merging into Cadeler, so there is no standalone sponsorship counterpart.
changed: Merged into Cadeler in 2024

name: Ransa
desc: Peruvian logistics operator providing warehousing, customs, transport and supply chain services to mining, retail and consumer companies.
markets: Logistics for corporate customers in Peru and several other Latin American countries, as part of Grupo Romero.
rationale: B2B logistics provider with regional footprint and little consumer brand; limited hospitality interest makes F1 fit weak.

name: Ruta del Este
desc: Panamanian toll road concession, Corredor Panama Este, operated by ISA Vias, collecting tolls on the Panama City east highway link.
markets: Drivers on one Panama toll road; owner ISA is a Colombian state-controlled power transmission group.
rationale: Single toll road project with no consumer marketing and no international ambitions; very unlikely sponsor.

name: SAIC Anji Logistics
desc: Logistics provider of SAIC Motor operating vehicle, parts and supply chain logistics for Chinese car makers and other customers.
markets: Moves vehicles and parts within China and exports cars by sea, including a car-carrier fleet.
rationale: Automotive logistics arm of a large car maker with international exports, though B2B and little marketing activity.

name: Alpenglow Rail
desc: Denver investment firm focused on short-line and regional freight railroads, operating or investing in rail assets.
markets: US-focused rail investor; details of holdings, scale and any markets beyond North America were not confirmed.
rationale: Investment vehicle with no consumer brand and unproven scale; very weak F1 relevance.

name: Grupo CICE
desc: Mexican logistics and port group running container terminals and logistics services; details are limited.
markets: Operates around the Veracruz port area in Mexico; international activity and plans were not confirmed.
rationale: B2B port operator with little known brand marketing; limited reason for F1 sponsorship.

name: Horizon Industrial Parks
desc: Indian developer of industrial and logistics parks, backed by Blackstone, with warehouses in multiple cities for e-commerce and logistics tenants.
markets: Tenants in Indian cities; ownership by Blackstone is international, but operations are in India only.
rationale: B2B warehouse landlord with institutional backing and no consumer marketing; little F1 relevance.

name: TVS Industrial & Logistics Parks
desc: Indian industrial and warehousing parks developer, part of the TVS Group and backed by Warburg Pincus.
markets: Warehouse tenants in Indian cities; no known operations or expansion plans outside India.
rationale: B2B warehouse landlord with no consumer marketing and domestic focus; weak F1 fit.

name: Invictus Investment
desc: Dubai commodities supply company sourcing food and agricultural products such as sugar and grain from producers for trading customers.
markets: Supplies traders in the Middle East and Africa; scale, ownership and any further markets were not confirmed.
rationale: B2B commodities trader without consumer brand; Gulf hospitality value is limited, so F1 fit is weak.

name: FreightCar America
desc: Maker of aluminium and steel railcars, producing coal, intermodal and other freight cars with manufacturing in Mexico.
markets: Sells railcars to North American railroads and lessors, manufacturing mainly in Mexico.
rationale: B2B railcar maker with a small customer base and little consumer visibility; weak F1 fit.

name: Wilson Sons
desc: Brazilian port, towage and logistics operator running tugboats, container terminals including Tecon Salvador and Rio Grande, and offshore support services.
markets: Serves shipping lines, importers, exporters and energy customers at Brazilian ports; no major operations outside Brazil.
rationale: Brazilian port group now inside MSC's orbit, which gives hospitality interest, but it is B2B and Brazil-focused.
changed: Acquired by MSC's SAS Shipping Agencies Services in 2024-25
f1: Owned by the MSC group, whose MSC Cruises is a current F1 partner; Wilson Sons itself has no confirmed F1 deal.

name: Hillwood Polska
desc: Polish arm of US developer Hillwood that develops and leases logistics and industrial parks and warehouses in Poland.
markets: Warehouse tenants in Poland; part of the Hillwood group of the United States, with no separate expansion confirmed.
rationale: B2B property developer with warehouse tenants and no consumer brand; limited reason for F1 sponsorship.

name: Shuk Herzl
desc: Supermarket chain described as specialising in fresh produce; store numbers and ownership were not confirmed.
markets: Appears to be an Israeli grocery retailer serving local shoppers; no international activity or plans confirmed.
rationale: Local grocery retailer with unconfirmed scale and no international reach; weak F1 fit.

name: Westshore Terminals Investment Corporation
desc: Owns and operates Westshore Terminals at Roberts Bank, British Columbia, the largest coal export terminal in North America.
markets: Handles coal and other bulk cargo from Canadian and US mines for shipment to Asian customers.
rationale: Single-asset B2B terminal owner with no consumer brand and a commodity focus; weak F1 relevance.

name: Reitar Logtech
desc: Hong Kong company listed on Nasdaq providing construction and logistics technology services; details of its products are limited.
markets: Appears to serve customers in Hong Kong; products, customers and any expansion plans are not confirmed.
rationale: Small listed Hong Kong B2B firm with unconfirmed business and no consumer brand; weak F1 fit.

name: Haoxin Holdings
desc: Freight forwarding and logistics company based in Beilun, Ningbo, apparently serving Chinese exporters; scale and clients are not confirmed.
markets: Based at the Ningbo port area in China; customers and overseas activity are not confirmed.
rationale: Small B2B freight forwarder with no consumer brand and unconfirmed scale; weak F1 relevance.

name: Dexus Australian Logistics Trust
desc: Unlisted fund established by Dexus to invest in logistics and industrial property in Australia.
markets: Invests in Australian logistics and industrial property; no operations outside Australia known.
rationale: Property fund vehicle with no operating brand to market; essentially unsuitable for a sponsorship.

name: LOGOS India
desc: Indian arm of LOGOS, an Asia-Pacific logistics real estate developer, building and leasing warehouses and industrial parks.
markets: Develops warehouses in Indian cities for e-commerce and logistics tenants; parent LOGOS operates across Asia-Pacific.
rationale: B2B warehouse developer with no consumer brand and India-only operations; weak F1 fit.

name: Singapore Post
desc: Singapore's national postal operator, delivering mail and parcels and running e-commerce logistics and freight forwarding businesses.
markets: Mail and parcels in Singapore plus e-commerce logistics and freight forwarding in Australia, Asia and other regions.
rationale: Well-known Singapore brand with a sizeable B2B customer base that could use the Singapore Grand Prix for hospitality.

name: GoGoX
desc: Hong Kong app-based on-demand logistics platform connecting customers with van and truck drivers for same-day delivery and moving.
markets: Delivery and moving services for businesses and consumers in Hong Kong and several other Asian markets.
rationale: Consumer-facing delivery app with regional Asian brand, but modest scale and no clear F1 tie-in.
changed: Renamed from GoGoVan to GoGoX

name: Instabox
desc: Stockholm e-commerce delivery company, now part of Instabee, offering parcel lockers and home delivery for online retailers.
markets: Delivers online orders for retailers in Sweden and neighbouring Nordic and European markets under the Instabee group.
rationale: Consumer-visible Nordic parcel brand, but regional delivery business with limited motorsport marketing relevance.
changed: Merged with Budbee into Instabee, announced 2022

name: LINE MAN Wongnai
desc: Thai super app combining LINE MAN food, grocery, ride and parcel delivery with the Wongnai restaurant review platform.
industry: delivery and local services super app
markets: Consumers and merchants across Thailand; no verified expansion beyond Thailand.
rationale: Consumer app with large Thai user base that could use F1 for activation, though Thailand-only and no Thai race.

name: ShipBob
desc: E-commerce fulfilment company offering a global network of warehouses plus software for storing, picking, packing and shipping online orders.
markets: Warehouses serve online brands in North America, Europe and Australia, selling to consumers worldwide.
rationale: B2B fulfilment brand for online sellers; some hospitality value for merchants but no strong consumer marketing, so fit is modest.

name: ShipMonk
desc: E-commerce fulfilment company offering warehousing, order fulfilment, returns and shipping for direct-to-consumer and Amazon sellers.
markets: Fulfilment centres in the United States, Europe and elsewhere serving online merchants.
rationale: B2B fulfilment provider with e-commerce seller customers; limited consumer brand and modest F1 hospitality value.

name: Fabric
desc: Commerce technology company that built automated micro-fulfilment centres to let grocers and retailers offer same-day delivery.
markets: Operated in the United States and Israel for retail customers before stopping operations in 2023.
rationale: Reportedly stopped operations in 2023, so there is no active partner to approach.
changed: Stopped operations in 2023

name: Enjoy
desc: Former mobile retail company founded by Ron Johnson that delivered products and set up devices with specialists at customers' doors.
markets: Operated in United States cities before failing; also expanded to the UK before its collapse.
rationale: Company went bankrupt and no longer operates, so no sponsorship is possible.
changed: Filed for bankruptcy in 2022

name: SF Express
desc: China's largest courier, offering express parcel delivery, freight, cold chain and international logistics through SF Holding.
markets: Domestic express network in China plus international express and freight services across Asia, Europe and North America.
rationale: Large Chinese logistics brand with growing international arm and hospitality value, though DHL already holds the F1 logistics role.

name: Alexandria Container and Cargo Handling Company
desc: Egyptian port operator at Alexandria port, handling container terminals, storage and cargo handling for shipping lines and importers.
markets: Container and cargo handling at Alexandria port in Egypt; no operations abroad known.
rationale: B2B port operator with no consumer brand and Egypt-only reach; weak F1 fit.

name: Bobst Group
desc: Swiss maker of machinery for the packaging industry, building die-cutting, folding-gluing, printing and corrugated and flexible packaging equipment.
markets: Sells packaging and label machinery to carton, label and packaging makers worldwide from Swiss and international plants.
rationale: Precision-engineering B2B brand with global customers and F1 technology overlap, though without consumer awareness.

name: 1mg
desc: Indian online pharmacy and healthcare platform offering medicine delivery, diagnostic lab tests and doctor consultations, part of Tata Digital.
markets: Consumers across India; owned by Tata Digital, with no verified operations abroad.
rationale: Large Indian health consumer brand, but India-only and health-product marketing is regulated, so F1 fit is weak.

name: Imperfect Foods
desc: Online grocery delivery company selling surplus and cosmetically imperfect produce plus pantry, meat and dairy items to US households.
markets: Consumers in United States metropolitan areas; no international operations.
rationale: US-only grocery delivery brand with a sustainability message but no international reach; weak F1 fit.

name: Bloom & Wild
desc: London online flower and gift delivery company, founded in 2013, known for letterbox flowers that fit through the letterbox.
markets: Consumers in the UK and several European countries including Germany and France.
rationale: Consumer gifting brand with seasonal occasions and European reach, but small scale and no obvious motorsport tie-in.

name: Hanjin
desc: South Korean logistics company, part of Hanjin Group, offering parcel delivery, freight forwarding, container transport and port services.
markets: Mainly serves customers in South Korea; overseas activity and expansion plans were not confirmed.
rationale: Korean logistics group with B2B customers; some hospitality use but domestic focus makes F1 fit weak.

name: Huolala
desc: On-demand logistics platform, also known as Lalamove, linking van, truck and motorcycle drivers with customers who need to move goods.
markets: Operates in China and in markets across Asia, Latin America and elsewhere under the Lalamove brand.
rationale: App-based consumer and SME delivery brand with international spread that could use F1 for brand visibility.

name: Dianwoda
desc: On-demand delivery company offering crowd-sourced last-mile and same-city delivery for restaurants, retailers and e-commerce through a rider app.
markets: Restaurants, retailers and e-commerce customers in Chinese cities; later tied to Alibaba's local services business.
rationale: China-only B2B delivery network with little consumer brand profile and no international reach; weak F1 fit.

name: Exotec
desc: French warehouse robotics company best known for the Skypod system, in which robots climb racks to pick and store items.
markets: Sells automated warehouse systems to retailers and manufacturers in Europe, North America and Asia.
rationale: Robotics unicorn with technology showcase value and growth ambitions in several regions; B2B hospitality for industrial customers.

name: Tembici
desc: Brazilian micromobility company running bike-sharing systems in cities including Sao Paulo, Rio de Janeiro, Santiago and Buenos Aires.
markets: Bike-sharing in Brazil, Chile and Argentina, often under naming sponsorships with local companies.
rationale: Urban mobility brand with consumer visibility in Latin American cities, but a modest budget and little obvious F1 link.

name: Castor Maritime
desc: Cyprus shipping company that owns and operates dry bulk vessels carrying iron ore, coal and grain for charterers.
markets: Charters vessels to commodity traders and miners on worldwide dry bulk routes.
rationale: Small B2B dry bulk shipowner with no consumer brand; F1 relevance is low.

name: SkyCell
desc: Zurich pharmaceutical logistics company that develops temperature-controlled shipping containers for transporting vaccines, biologics and other medicines.
markets: Container rental and monitoring for pharma shippers in Europe, the Americas, Asia and elsewhere.
rationale: Engineering-led cold-chain brand with a technology showcase angle, but B2B pharma customers limit marketing use.

name: Sindbad Overseas
desc: Omani shipping company in Muscat that charters commercial vessels and provides shipping services for cargo owners in the Gulf region.
markets: Serves cargo owners in the Gulf region; fleet, ownership and customers were not confirmed.
rationale: Low-profile B2B Omani shipper with no known marketing activity; weak F1 fit despite Gulf races.

name: Tampereen Ratikka
desc: Company that built and operates the Tampere tramway in Finland, a tram system opened in 2021 running through the city.
markets: Passengers in the Tampere region of Finland; no operations elsewhere.
rationale: Municipal tram project with no commercial marketing need and local reach only; very unlikely sponsor.

name: Li & Fung
desc: Hong Kong supply chain group, founded in 1906, sourcing apparel, home products and other consumer goods for retailers and brands.
industry: consumer goods sourcing and supply chain
markets: Sources goods in Asia for retail and brand customers in North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Long-established B2B sourcing group serving global fashion and retail brands, giving some hospitality value but little consumer marketing.

name: ID Logistics Group
desc: French contract logistics company offering warehousing, order preparation, transport management and e-commerce fulfilment for retailers and manufacturers.
markets: Runs warehouses for customers across Europe, the Americas, Asia and Africa in many countries.
rationale: International B2B logistics operator with retail clients suited to hospitality, though DHL and CEVA already occupy F1 logistics roles.

name: OceanPal
desc: Greek shipping company spun off from Diana Shipping in 2021, owning and operating dry bulk vessels chartered to commodity traders.
markets: Charters vessels to commodity traders and miners on worldwide dry bulk routes.
rationale: Small B2B dry bulk shipowner with no consumer brand; F1 relevance is low.
changed: Spun off from Diana Shipping in 2021

name: Imperial Petroleum
desc: Greek-run shipping company that owns and operates product tankers and crude vessels, chartering them to oil traders and energy firms.
markets: Charters tankers carrying refined petroleum products for traders and oil companies on international routes.
rationale: Small B2B tanker owner with no consumer brand and little marketing culture; F1 fit is weak.
changed: Spun off from StealthGas in 2021

name: ZPH
desc: Company based in Zhuhai, Guangdong, tagged by Crunchbase under energy, logistics and shipping; products and customers are not confirmed.
markets: Based in Zhuhai, China; customers, markets and any international activity are not confirmed.
rationale: Too little is known about the business or brand to see a clear F1 rationale.

name: Freight Technologies
desc: Digital freight brokerage, formerly Fr8Tech, whose Fr8App platform links shippers and truckers for cross-border freight between the US and Mexico.
markets: Shippers and truckers moving freight between the United States and Mexico, with operations centred on Mexico.
rationale: Small B2B logistics software firm with no consumer brand; weak F1 fit despite Mexican Grand Prix interest.
changed: Renamed from Fr8Tech to Freight Technologies

name: Globavend
desc: Cross-border e-commerce logistics company providing last-mile delivery and fulfilment for online sellers shipping from Asia to Australia and Europe.
markets: Moves parcels from Asia to Australia, the United Kingdom and Europe for online sellers.
rationale: Small B2B parcel logistics firm with no consumer brand and unconfirmed structure; weak F1 relevance.

name: Seanergy Maritime
desc: Greek shipping company owning Capesize dry bulk vessels that carry iron ore, coal and grain for charterers.
markets: Charters Capesize vessels to commodity traders, miners and steel groups on worldwide routes.
rationale: B2B dry bulk shipowner with no consumer brand; F1 relevance is low.

name: NIS
desc: Leading Serbian oil and gas company producing oil and gas, running the Pancevo refinery and selling fuels at filling stations.
markets: Fuel stations in Serbia and neighbouring Balkan states; majority owned by Gazprom Neft, which is under US sanctions.
rationale: Consumer-visible Serbian fuel brand, but Russian-owned and hit by US sanctions in 2025, which makes F1 partnership very unlikely.

name: Robin Energy
desc: Small shipping company operating product tankers that carry refined petroleum products for charterers.
markets: Charters a small fleet of tankers to oil traders and energy groups.
rationale: Tiny B2B tanker owner with no consumer brand; F1 fit is weak.

name: Icon Energy
desc: Athens shipping company in freight service and shipping, flagged by Crunchbase as listed; fleet and customers are not confirmed.
markets: Likely charters vessels to commodity or energy traders; fleet, ownership and markets were not confirmed.
rationale: Small B2B shipowner with no known consumer brand; F1 fit is weak.

name: Echo Global Logistics
desc: US third-party logistics provider arranging truckload, less-than-truckload, intermodal and managed transportation for shippers using a technology platform.
markets: Shippers across the United States; taken private and combined with Worldwide Express under WWEX Group.
rationale: B2B freight broker with no consumer brand and now part of a larger group; weak F1 fit.
changed: Taken private by The Jordan Company in 2021

name: Grupo EcoRodovias
desc: Brazilian infrastructure and logistics group operating toll road concessions in several states and port logistics in Santos.
markets: Motorists and cargo operators in Brazil; controlled by Argo Infrastructure Partners since 2022.
rationale: Brazilian toll road operator with road users as customers; modest hospitality interest and no international footprint.
changed: Acquired by Argo Infrastructure Partners in 2022

name: Belawan New Container Terminal
desc: Container terminal at Belawan port in Medan, North Sumatra, Indonesia, listed under logistics and supply chain.
markets: Handles containers for shipping lines and cargo owners in North Sumatra; owner and capacity were not confirmed.
rationale: Single port terminal with no consumer brand and unconfirmed ownership; very weak F1 fit.

name: Benlai
desc: Chinese fresh produce e-commerce platform, founded in 2012, selling fruit, vegetables, meat and seafood to urban consumers with cold-chain delivery.
markets: Households in Beijing and other big Chinese cities; no international operations known.
rationale: Chinese grocery e-commerce brand competing with larger rivals, domestic only, so F1 fit is weak.

name: Verastar
desc: UK services company in Sale, Cheshire, that sold business telecoms and related services to small businesses; current status is unconfirmed.
markets: Sold to UK small and medium businesses; current ownership and activity were not confirmed.
rationale: Status unclear and aimed at UK small business customers, so F1 sponsorship is very unlikely.

name: Gelato
desc: Print-on-demand platform connecting online sellers and brands with local print partners in about 30 countries to produce and ship products.
markets: Production network in about 30 countries serving e-commerce stores on platforms like Shopify and Etsy, and large brands.
rationale: International B2B platform with technology and creator-economy angle; moderate hospitality value for merchants and brand customers.

name: SiCepat Express
desc: Indonesian courier and last-mile delivery company, founded in 2014, providing express parcel delivery for online sellers and consumers.
markets: Parcel delivery across Indonesia for e-commerce sellers and consumers; no verified operations abroad.
rationale: Indonesian courier with consumer visibility but a single-country business, so F1 relevance is modest.

name: Waimai
desc: Former Baidu food delivery business in China, launched in 2014 and sold to Ele.me in 2017.
markets: Served Chinese consumers ordering from restaurants before Baidu sold it to Ele.me in 2017.
rationale: Brand no longer exists independently after its 2017 sale, so there is no sponsorship counterpart to approach.
changed: Sold by Baidu to Ele.me in 2017

name: Sendcloud
desc: Dutch shipping software company, founded in 2012, offering an all-in-one platform that connects online shops to many carriers.
markets: Online retailers across Europe use its platform to ship parcels with multiple carriers.
rationale: European B2B software firm with e-commerce customers; limited consumer brand, though technology tie-in offers some value.

name: Zongteng Network
desc: Shenzhen provider of cross-border logistics and shipping services helping Chinese e-commerce sellers ship goods to overseas buyers.
markets: Chinese online sellers shipping to buyers abroad through warehousing, freight forwarding and last-mile services; exact destinations not confirmed.
rationale: B2B cross-border logistics provider with little consumer brand; limited reason for F1 sponsorship.

name: Budbee
desc: Stockholm last-mile delivery company delivering online orders to homes, lockers and pickup points across the Nordics, the Netherlands and Belgium.
markets: Delivers for retailers in the Nordics, the Netherlands and Belgium; merged with Instabox into the Instabee group.
rationale: Consumer-visible Nordic delivery brand, but regional and part of Instabee, so F1 relevance is modest.
changed: Merged with Instabox into Instabee, announced 2022

name: Advanced Oncotherapy
desc: Medical technology company developing LIGHT, a compact linear accelerator meant to make proton therapy cheaper and more accessible for hospitals.
markets: Pre-revenue developer based in the UK; hospitals would be customers, but current status and markets are not confirmed.
rationale: Pre-revenue medical device developer with no consumer brand; weak F1 fit despite technology angle.

name: NewEase China
desc: Shanghai company that Crunchbase describes as an investor and operator of hubs, listed under logistics and warehousing.
markets: Based in Shanghai; customers, ownership and scale were not confirmed.
rationale: Unconfirmed B2B logistics hub operator with no known consumer brand; weak F1 relevance.

name: XPO
desc: Freight transportation company focused on less-than-truckload freight with terminals and trucks, after spinning off GXO and RXO in 2021.
markets: Industrial, retail and commercial shippers mainly in North America, with European transportation operations.
rationale: B2B freight brand with shipper hospitality value, but DHL and CEVA already hold F1 logistics roles and consumer awareness is low.
changed: Spun off GXO Logistics and RXO in 2021

name: Hyundai Glovis
desc: Logistics arm of Hyundai Motor Group running car-carrier fleets, finished vehicle logistics, contract logistics, bulk shipping and group parts distribution.
markets: Serves Hyundai, Kia and third-party shippers across several continents with car carriers and logistics hubs.
rationale: Large automotive logistics group tied to a major car maker, offering B2B hospitality for supply chain clients.

name: Thor Industries
desc: World's largest recreational vehicle maker, with brands such as Airstream, Jayco, Thor Motor Coach and, in Europe, Erwin Hymer Group.
markets: Sells RVs through dealers in North America and Europe under brands including Airstream, Jayco, Hymer and Dethleffs.
rationale: Consumer leisure brands in North America and Europe with US F1 audience overlap, though sold through dealers rather than direct.

name: CargoX
desc: Brazilian digital freight platform connecting shippers with truck drivers, handling road freight bookings, tracking and payments.
markets: Cargo owners and independent truck drivers in Brazil; restructured after its last funding in 2021, with current status unconfirmed.
rationale: B2B freight platform with no consumer brand and uncertain current status; weak F1 fit.

name: Emergent Cold
desc: Dallas temperature-controlled warehousing and logistics company building cold storage facilities for frozen and refrigerated goods.
markets: Cold storage for food producers, grocers and distributors, reportedly in North America and Latin America; scale unconfirmed.
rationale: B2B cold storage operator with no consumer brand and unconfirmed scale; F1 fit is weak.
